1. (Currently amended) A method, comprising: transmitting a sequence of modulated infrared light pulses having a first pulse rate to a vehicle; receiving a second sequence of modulated infrared light pulses from the vehicle, wherein the second sequence encodes vehicle state information; and transmitting a message as a sequence of modulated infrared light pulses having a second pulse rate based on the second sequence of light pulses received from the vehicle, wherein the first pulse rate is different from the second pulse rate, and wherein the message is transmitted only when the vehicle is within a predetermined proximity range and the vehicle state information indicates a safety-critical condition.

2. (Currently amended) The method of claim 1, wherein a computing device determines the second pulse rate based on the second sequence of light pulses received from the vehicle, the second pulse rate being slower than the first pulse rate, and wherein the computing device adjusts the second pulse rate dynamically in response to changes in the vehicle state information.

3. (Currently amended) The method of claim 2, wherein the computing device determines when the vehicle is no longer in the predetermined proximity range and transmits a sequence of modulated infrared light pulses having a third pulse rate, wherein the third pulse rate is faster than the second pulse rate and corresponds to a default transmission state.

4. (Currently amended) The method of claim 3, wherein the computing device receives a third sequence of modulated infrared light pulses from a third vehicle and transmits the message as a sequence of modulated infrared light pulses having a fourth pulse rate based on the third sequence of light pulses received from the third vehicle, wherein the fourth pulse rate is different from the second pulse rate and is determined based on the vehicle state information from the third vehicle.

5. (Original) The method of claim 1, wherein the light pulses are modulated IR radiation.

6. (Currently amended) The method of claim 1, wherein the message includes information regarding vehicle position, motion, size, safety events, path history and vehicle status, encoded into light pulses as binary bits, wherein the encoding is independent of message transmission pulse rate, and wherein the message is transmitted only via modulated infrared light pulses and not via wireless vehicle-to-vehicle network protocols.

7. (Cancelled)

8. (Currently amended) The method of claim 1, wherein the sequences of modulated infrared light pulses are received via an infrared video sensor that captures and decodes the modulated signals.

9. (Currently amended) The method of claim 1, wherein the sequences of modulated infrared light pulses are received from two or more vehicles simultaneously within the predetermined proximity range.

10. (Currently amended) The method of claim 9, further comprising: emitting the message as a sequence of modulated infrared light pulses having a fourth pulse rate based on the sequences of light pulses, wherein the fourth pulse rate is set equal to the slowest of the sequences of light pulses received from the two or more vehicles.
